changes: First PeerConnection close owner starts a one-second timer; stalled final transport writes trigger ICE Stop and the timer worker is joined before returning.
Normal close ordering and all live transport behavior remain unchanged.
The existing sender-associated RTCP and FlexFEC receiver extensions are retained in one published fork revision.
Native ICE-restart test buffers candidates until the matching remote SDP is applied; later candidates are still forwarded immediately.
Local distributor signaling fixtures use IPv4/IPv6 loopback candidates and register cleanup as soon as each peer is created. Production interface selection is unchanged.

limitations: The original unrestricted-interface macOS full native suite timed out while MassiveTracks awaited a connection, before Close was called; the isolated test passed.
The original distributor restart still failed with the shutdown fix alone, but cleanup completed instead of hanging. Loopback fixture success does not establish external IPv6 restart success.
The one-second grace interrupts blocked transport I/O; it is not a universal bound for arbitrary application callbacks, custom network implementations or every possible lock deadlock.
Passing local suites and MediaMTX integration do not supersede retained impaired-network, TURN-loss or periodic presentation-freeze failures.
